parts:
Hi Jefe,

If you have too many labels, don't print them all:


p + scale_x_continuous("", breaks=c(1, 3),
labels = as.Date(c("2010-06-03", "2010-06-07")))

you can also angle them to make more room:


p + scale_x_continuous("", breaks=c(1, 3),
labels = as.Date(c("2010-06-03", "2010-06-07"))) +
theme(axis.text=element_text(angle = 70, hjust=1))

Best,
Ista

> I need to create a standard finance style graph, in which I have say 10 days
> daily price data over two weeks to plot. But, the data is irregular, in that

>
> The following code works fine, and illustrates the graph I do want to
> produce.
>
> The problem arises when I have say 20 or 30 or 200 days to plot, the x-axis
> labels overprint looking awful; is there a way to overcome this;
> Standard R graphics will cope with the labels perfectly with this approach,
> I am surprised ggplot does not..
>
> library(ggplot2)
> p <- qplot(1:3, 1:3, geom='line')
> p + scale_x_continuous("", breaks=1:3,
> labels = as.Date(c("2010-06-03", "2010-06-04", "2010-06-07")))
>
> ggsave(file="egSimple.png", dpi=300)
>
> Thanks for suggestions

> Jefe
